package_info.package_manager: custom/third-party JavaScript (not npm, but included as a static asset)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is considered malicious because attackers injected additional JavaScript code into the end of a widely used library (modernizr), turning it into a vehicle for skimming payment form data and exfiltrating credit card details from users. This code was not part of the legitimate library and was used to compromise sensitive user data at scale.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when payment form is loaded and used by the victim in the browser)
execution_context.file_location: modernizr.js (appended to the end of the legitimate library, served as a static asset on the website)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code attaches an event listener to the payment form's submit event, collects all form data (including credit card details), and sends it via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled domain, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior is suspicious because it intercepts sensitive user input (payment details) and exfiltrates it to an external domain not associated with the legitimate business.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior for a JavaScript library like modernizr is to provide feature detection utilities, not to access payment forms or transmit user data to third-party domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or payment processors may collect form data, but only to trusted, documented endpoints and with user consent.
key_indicators: Code appended to a widely used third-party library
Event listener on payment form submission
Exfiltration of form data to an external, non-canonical domain
Use of fetch/XMLHttpRequest to send sensitive data

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits an unpatched Magento installation to gain access to the web server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to modify static assets served to users.

attack_chain.action: Attacker appends malicious JavaScript code to the end of the modernizr.js library.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is served to all users visiting the payment page.

attack_chain.action: When a user loads the payment page, the malicious code executes in their browser, intercepts payment form submissions, and exfiltrates data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives credit card and personal data from victims.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code in static assets that attaches event listeners to payment forms
Outbound network requests from payment pages to untrusted or unexpected domains
Unexpected modifications or appended code in third-party libraries
file_indicators: modernizr.js with appended or altered code not present in the official release
Static asset files with recent unauthorized changes
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests from client browsers to domains not associated with the legitimate business (e.g., malicious-domain.com/collect)
Unusual traffic patterns from payment pages to external endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor static assets for unauthorized changes by comparing deployed files to known-good hashes. Inspect JavaScript on payment pages for event listeners on forms that send data to external domains. Use Content Security Policy (CSP) to restrict outbound requests from sensitive pages. Monitor network traffic for POST requests to unknown domains originating from payment or checkout pages.
